newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to name woman, scholar in new cabinet - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to name woman, scholar in new cabinet - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's government, eager to regain public confidence lost due to a crime wave, plans to name its first female interior minister when it unveils a cabinet reshuffle next week, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
Premier Lien Chan will appoint Yeh Ching-feng, minister without portfolio, to head the Interior Ministry, the China Times newspaper said, quoting unidentified official sources.

Incumbent Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng resigned on Thursday after coming under fire for the island's worsening crime levels that culminated in the kidnap and murder of the teenage daughter of popular Taiwan actress Pai Ping-ping.
Public anger with crime sparked calls for the resignation of President Lee Teng-hui and Premier Lien Chan. The government has responded by announcing it would reshuffle the cabinet next Wednesday.
Two other cabinet-level ministers -- Ma Ying-jeou, minister without portfolio, and Tjiu Mau-ying, chairman of Taiwan's Council of Agriculture -- also resigned on the same day as Lin.

The newspaper said Lien, who has not approved Ma's resignation, would try to persuade him to stay on. The popular Ma, who as justice minister gained a reputation as a graft-buster, has been touted as one of the ruling Nationalist party's rising stars

Tjiu has been under fire since March for the Council of Agriculture's failure to prevent the outbreak of a deadly epidemic of hog foot-and-mouth disease that forced Taiwan to ban pork exports, jeopardising the island's fragile economic recovery.
Tjiu would be replaced by agriculture expert Peng Tso-kuei, the China Times said.

Hsu Chieh-kwei, vice minister of transportation and communications, would succeed Hsieh Shen-shan as Council of Labour Affairs chairman, the paper said. Hsieh stepped down last month to run in the Taipei County magistrate election.
